topicName: Vacuum Internals, Bloat Management, and Autotuning
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"PostgreSQL Vacuum Internals, Bloat Management, and Autotuning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) to handle concurrent transactions. When rows are updated or deleted, the old versions are not immediately removed from physical storage. Instead, they remain as dead tuples, leading to table and index bloat over time. Understanding Vacuum internals and properly configuring autotuning parameters is critical for maintaining database health and performance."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding MVCC and Dead Tuples"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In PostgreSQL, an UPDATE operation is executed as a DELETE followed by an INSERT. This leaves behind a dead tuple in the data page. Until these dead tuples are cleaned up, sequential scans must read bloated pages, which wastes I/O bandwidth and degrades performance. The VACUUM process reclaims this storage, marking dead tuple space as reusable for future inserts."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"How VACUUM Internals Work"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 1: Scanning the heap for dead tuples and building an in-memory list of dead tuple locations."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 2: Scanning indexes associated with the table to remove index pointers pointing to those dead tuples."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 3: Vacuuming the heap by clearing dead tuples and updating the Free Space Map (FSM) and Visibility Map (VM)."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Identifying Table and Index Bloat"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can monitor dead tuples and table bloat using system catalogs and views like pg_stat_user_tables. The following query helps identify tables with high volumes of dead tuples:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT schemaname, relname, n_dead_tup, n_live_tup, round(100.0 * n_dead_tup / nullif(n_dead_tup + n_live_tup, 0), 2) AS dead_tuple_pct FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE (n_dead_tup + n_live_tup) > 10000 ORDER BY dead_tuple_pct DESC;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Autotuning Configuration Parameters"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Default autotuning settings in PostgreSQL are optimized for small, out-of-the-box databases and often fail on high-throughput, large-scale production systems. You must adjust parameters in postgresql.conf to trigger vacuuming more aggressively."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"autotuning_vacuum_scale_factor: Determines the fraction of table size added before a vacuum is triggered (default is 0.2 or 20%). Lower this to 0.05 (5%) for large, busy tables."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"autotuning_vacuum_threshold: Minimum number of updated or deleted tuples needed to trigger a vacuum. Combine this with a lower scale factor."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"autotuning_vacuum_cost_limit and autotuning_vacuum_cost_delay: Control throttling to prevent VACUUM from consuming excessive I/O. Increase the cost limit on modern hardware with SSDs."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Per-Table Autotuning Configuration"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"For critical tables that experience high update frequency, you can override global autotuning settings directly on the table:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"ALTER TABLE high_traffic_orders SET (autotuning_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.05, autotuning_vacuum_threshold = 1000);"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Severe Bloat with VACUUM FULL and pg_repack"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard VACUUM does not return disk space to the operating system; it only marks space as available in the FSM for the same table. If a table has severe structural bloat, standard vacuuming is insufficient. While VACUUM FULL reclaims space and defragments the table, it acquires an exclusive lock, blocking all reads and writes. For zero-downtime bloat remediation in production, utilize the external extension pg_repack."}]
